title: Keyboard: Tab order follows a logical sequence
steps: Focus the page (click anywhere or press Tab until focus appears)
Press `Tab` repeatedly to move forward through interactive elements until end of page
Press `Shift+Tab` repeatedly to move backward through interactive elements
expectedResults: Focus moves in a clear, logical order that matches the visual layout (left-to-right, top-to-bottom)
No interactive control is skipped during Tab or Shift+Tab navigation
Focusable order does not trap keyboard (user can reach all interactive controls and page end)

title: Keyboard: All controls operable by keyboard
preconditions: Page loaded and focusable elements discoverable
steps: Tab to the 'new todo' input and type a todo text
Press `Enter` to add the todo
Tab to the todo item's checkbox or toggle and press `Space` or `Enter` to toggle completion
Tab to the delete button/icon and press `Enter` or `Space` to delete the todo
expectedResults: User can add a todo using keyboard alone
User can toggle todo complete/incomplete using keyboard
User can delete a todo using keyboard
Action responses happen without requiring mouse interaction

title: ARIA: Page uses correct landmark roles and ARIA attributes
steps: Inspect page source or using accessibility tree to find `role="banner"` or `<header>` for top area
Verify presence of `role="main"` or `<main>` for the primary content
Verify presence of `role="contentinfo"` or `<footer>` for footer area
Inspect todo list region for appropriate role (e.g., `list`, `listitem`) and interactive controls for `role` and `aria-*` attributes
expectedResults: Header has a landmark (`header` or `role='banner'`)
Main content uses `main` or `role='main'`
Footer uses `footer` or `role='contentinfo'`
Todo list is exposed as a list to assistive tech (`role='list'` and children `role='listitem'`) or semantically via `<ul>/<li>`
Interactive controls expose role and state (e.g., `aria-checked` for checkboxes if custom, `aria-label` for icon-only buttons)

title: ARIA: Name, Role, Value are available to AT (4.1.2) for interactive elements
steps: Using accessibility inspector (browser DevTools > Accessibility or external tool), check the accessible name, role and value for:
- New todo input
- Add/submit action (if separate)
- Todo item toggle/checkbox
- Delete button/icon
expectedResults: Each interactive element exposes an accurate accessible name (from label, aria-label, aria-labelledby or visible text)
Each control exposes an appropriate role (e.g., textbox, button, checkbox, listitem)
When stateful, value/state is exposed (e.g., `aria-checked` for custom toggle)

title: Form fields: 'new todo' input has an associated label
steps: Inspect the `new todo` input element
Check for a visible label, `label[for]` association, or `aria-label`/`aria-labelledby`
Try to read label via screen reader or accessibility tree
expectedResults: The `new todo` input has an accessible name provided by a visible label or `aria-label`/`aria-labelledby`
Screen reader announces the input's purpose when focused

title: Color contrast: Text and UI controls meet 4.5:1 contrast (1.4.3)
preconditions: Page loaded; developer tools or color contrast tool available
steps: Identify body text, headings, and interactive element text (buttons, links)
Measure contrast ratio between text color and background color using a contrast tool for: normal text (>=4.5:1) and large text (>=3:1)
Measure non-text contrast of important UI components (focus indicators, icons) if relevant
expectedResults: All normal-size text meets contrast ratio >= 4.5:1
Large text (>= 18pt or 14pt bold) meets >= 3:1
Essential UI components have sufficient non-text contrast per WCAG 2.1 AA (1.4.11) where applicable

title: Focus visibility: Focus indicator is visible and meets contrast requirements
steps: Tab to interactive elements (input, todos, buttons)
Observe the visible focus indicator (outline, box-shadow, background change)
Check that the focus indicator is clearly visible against the surrounding content and meets visual contrast where it relies on color
expectedResults: When an element receives keyboard focus, a visible focus indicator is present
Focus indicator is not hidden or only visible on hover
Focus indicator contrast ensures visibility for low-vision users (clear boundary and color/shape)
Focus is not lost after dynamic DOM updates (e.g., after adding a todo) unless intentionally moved

title: Images and icons: Provide alternative text or accessible names (1.1.1)
preconditions: Page loaded; inspect images/icons used in UI
steps: Locate any images or icon-only buttons (e.g., delete icon)
Check for `alt` text on images or `aria-label`/`aria-labelledby` on icon-only buttons
For decorative images, confirm `alt=""` or role/presentation
expectedResults: Images conveying information have descriptive `alt` text
Decorative images are marked decorative (`alt=""` or proper role/presentation)
Icon-only buttons provide accessible names via `aria-label` or visible text

title: Landmarks: Header, main and footer exist and are discoverable
steps: Inspect page for `<header>`, `<main>`, and `<footer>` elements or roles `banner`, `main`, `contentinfo`
Use a screen reader or accessibility tree to jump between landmarks
Verify that the primary todo app content is within `main` landmark
expectedResults: Page includes header (banner), main (main content) and footer (contentinfo) landmarks
Users can navigate directly to main landmark using AT landmark navigation
Landmarks are used semantically to represent page regions

title: Screen reader: Announce dynamic changes (aria-live) when todos are added, completed, or deleted
preconditions: Page loaded; screen reader available or accessibility tree inspection tool
steps: Enable a screen reader or use tools that emulate AT announcements
Add a new todo and observe for announcement
Mark a todo complete/incomplete and observe for announcement
Delete a todo and observe for announcement
expectedResults: When a todo is added, an accessible announcement is made (e.g., via `aria-live` region) describing the action and item
When a todo is toggled completed/incomplete, the new state is announced
When a todo is deleted, an announcement confirms deletion
Announcements are concise and do not interrupt unnecessarily (correct `aria-live` level used)

title: Dynamic components: Focus management after adding or deleting todos
steps: Focus the `new todo` input, type a todo, press Enter to add
Observe where keyboard focus lands after add
Delete a todo using keyboard, observe focus after deletion
Repeat adding multiple todos and deleting the last item
expectedResults: After adding a todo, focus remains on the input or moves to a predictable and documented location (e.g., newly added item) — consistent behavior
After deletion focus moves to a logical place (e.g., next todo, previous todo, or a meaningful control) and is not lost
No unexpected focus traps occur during dynamic updates

title: Semantic HTML: Use native controls where possible (buttons, inputs, lists)
steps: Inspect markup for use of semantic elements: `<button>`, `<input>`, `<ul>/<li>`
If custom elements are used (div/span as button), inspect for appropriate `role`, keyboard handlers and accessible name
Test those custom controls with keyboard and screen reader
expectedResults: Native controls are used for actions where possible
If custom controls are used, they expose correct `role`, keyboard behavior and accessible name/value/state
Assistive technology interacts with custom controls as expected

title: Forms and errors: No hidden validation barriers and errors are announced
steps: Attempt to submit an empty todo if the app prevents empty todos
Observe any validation message and whether it is visible and announced
Check whether validation message links to the invalid input or focuses it
expectedResults: If input is invalid, a clear visible error message is shown
Error is programmatically associated with the input (`aria-describedby`) and announced by screen readers
User can find and correct the error using keyboard and AT

title: Color-only information: No instructions or state rely solely on color
steps: Identify instances where color indicates state (e.g., completed todo greyed out)
Check whether there is an additional visual indicator (icon, text, strike-through) and programmatic state
Verify that assistive tech can perceive state (aria-checked, aria-pressed, text)
expectedResults: State is not conveyed by color alone; an additional cue (e.g., strike-through, `aria-checked`) is present
Screen readers announce state changes
Users with color vision deficiency can perceive all required information
